title: Chapter 33 — The Psychology of the Ask
intro: Why salespeople don't ask for the business, why customers need them to, and closing as a service.

sections.title: Why We Don't Ask
sections.content:
Most salespeople do not lose sales because they cannot handle objections. They lose sales because they never ask for the business in the first place.

The fear of rejection stops more closes than price, competition, or timing combined. We present beautifully. We demo perfectly. We answer every question. And then we wait for the customer to say 'I will take it' — which they almost never do on their own.

Closing is not pushy. It is a service. The customer came in because they need an appliance. They spent 30 minutes with you because they are interested. They are waiting for you to guide them to the decision. When you do not ask, you leave them in limbo — and they leave your store without buying.

sections.title: Closing as a Service
sections.content:
Think of it this way. If a doctor examined you, diagnosed the problem, and then said 'well, let me know if you want to do something about it' — you would be confused. You would want the doctor to say 'here is what I recommend and here is the next step.'

You are the appliance doctor. You diagnosed their needs. You prescribed the right product. Now tell them the next step. 'I think this is the right one for you. Should I get the paperwork started?'

That is not pushy. That is professional.

sections.title: The Timing of the Ask
sections.content:
Ask after the demo, not before. Ask after you have addressed their main concern, not while it is still hanging. Ask when they show buying signals — not when you are anxious to close.

If you did Steps 1 through 7 right, the close should feel natural. If it feels forced, you skipped something. Go back. Re-discover. Re-demo. Then ask.
